metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude runs an email-sequence skill, does it just write you one good email, or does it design the whole multi-email flow around it? Lands the carry-out that email-sequence hands back the whole sequence -- copy, timing, branches, exit conditions -- built the same way every time.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed the skill just writes one email. It doesn't — it designs the whole sequence: timing between sends, branching logic, exit conditions. So: does Claude write one email?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Does Claude write one email?', hesitates on 'email', corrects to 'sequence', lands the real question

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is email-sequence. Its SKILL.md file holds the full instruction set, in plain language — no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The instructions are laid out in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and runs it — linear, no branching unless a step says otherwise.

Here's the actual job: design and draft the full multi-email sequence — the copy for every message, the timing between sends, branching logic for opens and clicks, exit conditions, and benchmarks to judge it by. Built for onboarding, lead nurture, win-back, re-engagement, and launch flows.
Ask it for an email, and email-sequence hands back the whole sequence — copy, timing, branches, exit conditions — built the same way every time.

props.sparkLine: One ask in. The whole sequence out.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I'm launching a two-week free trial for my product. Design a five-email onboarding sequence — send timing for each, one branch for someone who never opens the first email, and an exit condition once they upgrade. Walk me through the sequence before you write the copy. That clause matters — explaining first surfaces the real constraint logic.
